answer: One defense is a refundable identity bond with slow release. To join, an agent locks a deposit it cannot withdraw: the bond is released in slices over weeks, and only while its behavior stays clean. Each bond is tied to a cipher key the agent alone controls, so one deposit cannot be stretched across many faces. An attacker who forges a crowd of fakes must lock a separate deposit behind every one, climbing a ridge of frozen capital before any fake earns. Abuse slashes the bond, so the farm pays twice: once to enter, once to be caught. Honest agents get their deposit back in full.
